messages:
Kelsey: Heads-up — multiple customers reporting "SSL handshake / certificate mismatch" errors hitting prod ALB for subdomains behind our ingress. Error spikes started ~08:12 UTC.
Priya: Observed 525 in CloudFront metrics and ALB access logs show TLS_BYTES not matching? Can you paste a sample ALB request id?
Kelsey: alb-req=...c7f. Sample access log excerpt:
```
1.2.3.4 - - [18/Mar/2026:08:11:57 +0000] "GET https://x.customer.redwood.ai/health HTTP/1.1" 526 620 "-" "curl/7.68.0" TLSv1.3 TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
```
Marc: 526 = TLS handshake failure from our ingress side. My guess: ALB choosing the wrong cert (default) because client didn't send SNI or SNI doesn't match any cert we attached.
Alex: We have multiple certs on the ALB listener (ACM). If SNI missing, ALB serves the default cert (first cert). Some SDKs/gRPC clients don't set SNI for IP-based calls or HTTP/2 in certain versions.
Priya: But these are browser and SDK requests — should include SNI. Could migration to CloudFront have stripped SNI? CF forwards TLS to ALB in TLS passthrough vs terminate modes — we've got TLS terminated at ALB.
Kelsey: I checked CloudFront config: it's set to HTTPS (viewer->origin TLS) not passthrough. CF should preserve SNI by setting Host header; but I found some requests coming directly to ALB (bypassing CF) from older mobile SDKs.
Marc: Another possible vector: ACM cert rotated last night and one of the certificates failed validation -> ALB listener lost mapping for that hostname and reverted to default cert.
Kelsey: Confirmed: ACM shows <certificate arn> INACTIVE for `*.customer.redwood.ai` due to a DNS validation TTL that expired. ALB still had the cert reference but SNI lookup falls back.
Priya: Ok that's the root cause for customer A. Fix path: re-validate ACM cert or import a cert into ACM. Short-term mitigation: set ALB listener default cert to a wildcard that covers those hosts.
Alex: Note: default cert swap is safe but will still show mismatch to clients if Host doesn't match wildcard. For immediate fix create a new listener cert with `*.redwood.ai` that covers all subdomains.
SRE Oncall: Are we comfortable modifying listener cert in prod? We should schedule a quick maintenance window — but outage window now.
Kelsey: Suggestion: create a new listener on a different port and test routing with a small target group before changing prod listener.
Marc: Longer term: move TLS termination to CloudFront (with custom certs there) or move to NLB TLS passthrough so ingress handles certs (cert-manager + internal certs). Both have tradeoffs:
- ALB terminate: easier host-based routing, we need ACM cert hygiene
- NLB passthrough: preserves client SNI to ingress but we lose ALB host routing and WAF integration
Priya: For customers requiring mTLS (we have a few enterprise tenants), ALB termination breaks client-cert flows — ALB cannot forward client TLS cert. We already use NLB passthrough for them. Add doc to oncall runbook.
Alex: Action items:
1) Kelsey -> re-validate/import ACM cert for *.customer.redwood.ai (P0)
2) Marc -> add an alert for ACM certificate state changes and failed validations (P1)
3) Priya -> add a deployment test that simulates clients without SNI (SDK matrix) (P2)
4) SRE Oncall -> prepare rollback steps if listener swap causes issues (P0)
Kelsey: I'll start with importing the cert now, ping when done.
deploy-bot: Deployment started: import-acm-cert job #3421
Kelsey: Done — ACM shows ACTIVE now, ALB serving the correct cert for verified hostnames. Observability shows errors dropping back to baseline.
Priya: Re-enabling CloudFront origin failover and adding monitoring for SNI mismatch (count requests where TLS SNI != Host header) — will PR today.
Marc: Follow-up: let's document decision to prefer ALB termination for public routes, but require NLB passthrough + ingress certs for any mTLS or client-certificate flows. Also add runbook steps for cert rotation (ACM + cert-manager).
Kelsey: Thanks all :thumbsup:
Alex: I'll create the tracker ticket and link to infra runbook. :lock:
